Situation1: Your friend has misunderstood the tone of your text message and replied sounding hurt. You need to call them right now to explain.
Expectation2: Greet clients and make them feel comfortable
Situation2: A bride-to-be and her entourage arrive early, visibly anxious about the tight wedding schedule.
Story: My phone buzzes just as I’m sweeping up stray hair from the last client. It’s Mia—my best friend. Her message is clipped, her words sharp. She thinks I was annoyed with her, but I was just rushing between clients. I know I should call her right now, clear things up before the misunderstanding festers. That’s what friends do: talk things out, don’t let hurt feelings linger. But as I reach for my phone, the salon door swings open. The bride-to-be and her bridesmaids file in, all nerves and excitement, glancing at the clock. I’m supposed to greet them, make them feel at ease, set the tone for their big day. My heart pounds. I can’t leave Mia hanging, but I can’t ignore the anxious faces in front of me either. I feel split in two, torn between the friend who needs reassurance and the professional who’s expected to be calm and welcoming. My hand hovers over my phone, my mind racing, caught between two worlds that both need me right now.
